reading.body:
This facility publishes 2.65 MW of critical load UPS capacity across 44,550 square feet in downtown Salt Lake City. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this represents roughly 66 racks of compute; at hyperscale density of 100 kW per rack, roughly 27 racks. The published certifications qualify the building to host regulated workloads including government controlled information (ITAR) and financial payment systems (PCI DSS), though which customers currently occupy the space is not published.

In Utah's published data center capacity, this facility ranks sixth by megawatts among the nine facilities that publish figures. Utah's nine mapped operators disclose 52.18 MW total, making this single downtown Salt Lake City site represent 5.1% of the state's published IT capacity. The state has 21 mapped facilities overall, indicating most operators publish no capacity figure to this site.

The facility's size and certifications place it in the category of enterprise and regulated-workload hosting rather than AI infrastructure scale. For an AI campus assessment, the 2.65 MW figure is small relative to the hyperscaler builds now shaping compute availability, and no published power supply redundancy, cooling architecture, or grid connection details are available to assess whether this site could expand or support higher-density workloads.
